title: Actionable incident cards + cost-aware rollout controls for private clusters
creator: Ariana Cho
description: Design a compact, action-first incident card and an integrated rollout control surface for Private/VPC clusters that surfaces estimated cost impact, recommended rollback or model-variant actions, and one-click mitigations. The aim is to reduce time-to-mitigation for tenant-facing degradations while making cost trade-offs explicit to SREs and platform teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Incident cards appear in the Private Cluster 'Status' panel and show: incident title, severity, affected tenants, brief root-cause hints, and an estimated incremental cost delta (last 24h vs baseline).
2) Each card exposes primary actions: Add to Canary, Pause Rollout, Trigger Fallback Variant, Open Debug Shell (link), and Mark Investigating. Actions must include confirmation flows where destructive.
3) Rollout controls allow cost-aware canaries: step size, max cost delta per step, automated pause-on-cost-threshold.
4) Prototype validated in user testing with at least 5 SRE/platform engineers and 3 PM customers; task completion time for 'pause rollout and rollback' reduced by 40% vs current flow.
5) All links in cards resolve to existing tools: GitHub PRs, runbooks (Confluence), logs (Grafana/Loki), and the cluster-trace view.
design_notes:
- Use compact 3-line summary layout for cards to avoid vertical noise in the Status page.
- Cost metric uses internal 'delta-cost' calc from Optimize team (est. USD/hour) and shows color-coded delta: neutral (<1%), warning (1-5%), critical (>5%).
- Primary actions are contextual: if a rollout is active, show Pause/Abort; if model variant fallback exists, surface it with a confidence score.
- Add a small 'why this costs more' tooltip that lists contributors (batch size, fallback model, increased QPS).
- Mobile and tablet: collapse extra details behind a chevron; primary action must remain single-tap.
- Accessibility: each card must be navigable by keyboard, with ARIA labels for actions.
decisions:
1) Show estimated cost delta with two decimals and currency symbol (USD).
2) Implement color rules for delta bands as described above.
3) Action 'Trigger Fallback Variant' will call the existing runtime API implemented by ENG-2201; design will include a confirmation modal with rollback preview.
4) We will not surface raw billing numbers for multi-currency customers in this phase—only normalized USD deltas.
5) Rollout 'auto-pause on cost' default is OFF; turned on via cluster policy (PM decision).
tradeoffs:
- Surface financial signals too aggressively and we risk alert fatigue; too conservatively and teams miss cost regressions. We chose explicit deltas with thresholds to balance noise.
- Exposing cost numbers in the incident flow requires careful permissions; initial rollout restricts detailed cost drilldown to users with billing view permissions (de-scoped for current prototype).
- One-click mitigations accelerate fixes but increase risk of human error; mitigated via confirmation modals and brief runbook links.
review_feedback: ENG (Samir Patel): Prototype looks actionable; request: add an API contract note for rollback safety checks (ENG-2234).
PM (Jia Nguyen): Love the cost delta, request that we add an optional annotation field so PMs can tag incidents with customer-impact notes.
SRE (Leah Torres): Concern about exposing 'Open Debug Shell' by default; recommend it be gated behind an 'advanced' toggle.
